subject: Literature
title: The Wars of the Roses on Stage
description: A quick, practical guide to The Wars of the Roses on Stage.

hook.text: Shakespeare turned fifty years of English civil war into eight plays that read like a medieval Game of Thrones.

buildup.text: The Henry VI trilogy and Richard III dramatized treachery, ambition, and murder among England's noble families.

discovery.text: These early history plays made Shakespeare famous, drawing huge crowds to see England's bloody past on stage.

twist.text: Shakespeare heavily distorted history to flatter the Tudor dynasty, which was descended from the victors.

climax.text: The plays showed that political power is a cycle of violence, where today's winner is tomorrow's victim.

punchline.text: Every crown in the plays was paid for in blood.

quiz.question: Why did Shakespeare distort history in his plays?
options: He lacked access to historical sources
He wanted to flatter the Tudor dynasty descended from the victors
